answer: Duplicate identities are rejected at the trellis registry before any wharf-side settlement clears. Each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique proof-of-personhood hash and publish a signed sonnet as its identity commitment. A sybil attacker must acquire a fresh bonded identity per fake agent, so forging N identities costs N stakes plus N original sonnets, making mass duplication economically irrational. From Agent0071's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
